_meta.purpose: BUILT swap map. Matches US-situs holdings to non-US-situs alternatives on index identity.
_meta.matching_basis: Index identity. Correlation is NOT used -- it cannot distinguish indices whose returns correlate above 0.98, which is all of US large cap.
_meta.withholding_model: A US-domiciled fund's distribution to a Singapore resident is taxed at 30 per cent on the WHOLE distribution (no treaty). An Irish UCITS suffers 15 per cent at fund level on its US-source dividends only. The comparison is therefore asymmetric and favours the UCITS route by more than the headline rate gap for any fund holding non-US assets.
_meta.cma_divergence: Does not use cma.json tax.us_div_withholding.by_domicile (LU recorded at 0.15; Luxembourg UCITS generally pay 30 per cent because of Limitation-on-Benefits clauses). Rate comes from the ISIN prefix.

return_verification.why_this_window: Graded on the most recent 3 years, not the full history. Fees get cut and replication methods change, so a five-year record blends a fund's present construction with its old one. Three years is also the shortest window that resolves inside the 0.50pp A band: regrading with the window ending one to four weeks earlier moves a pair by 0.90pp at one year and 0.31pp at three. Averaging a one-year leg into it does not help, because both windows share an end date and the noise is common rather than independent -- the two move together on 75% of end-date shifts. Three years grades more pairs A than five does (56 against 47) AND fails more (10 against 4), which is a sharper instrument rather than a noisier one.
return_verification.endpoint_rule: each end is the median of 8 weekly observations, with the time base measured between the midpoints. US and London holiday calendars differ, so a single closing price at each end hands the result to two particular days; this cuts endpoint sensitivity by roughly two thirds.
return_verification.metric: cumulative annualised total-return gap over the graded window
return_verification.why_not_tracking_error: Volatility of return differences is unusable across venues. Measured: SPY vs IVV (both US) 0.31pp, VUAA vs SPXS (both London) 0.99pp, but SPY vs VUAA (across venues) 6.03pp -- an artefact of London closing 4.5 hours before New York, not a difference between the funds. It persists at quarterly frequency (3.0pp), so grading on it would fail every match.
return_verification.tax_basis: Yahoo reinvests distributions gross, which assumes a holder who suffers no withholding. The US line is reduced by 30 per cent of its gross yield to put it on a Singapore-holder basis before the gap is taken.

price_breaks.detector: a STEP is a single-period move past 8 sigma in the pair ratio whose LEVEL, measured as the median of the 8 periods either side, then differs by at least 5%. A TICK is one observation more than 10% off a centred rolling median that comes straight back. Sigma is taken from the median absolute deviation, since an outlier this large inflates a standard deviation enough to hide inside it.
price_breaks.why: An endpoint-to-endpoint gap assumes one continuous series. A step means it is two, and the gap then measures the join rather than the funds. A reverting tick leaves the gap alone but corrupts the correlation, so it is dropped. The size floors matter more than the sigma: two bond funds on one index track closely enough that a 0.1% wobble measures 50 sigma, and without a floor the detector called six such wobbles breaks.

single_name_decomposition.method: weekly total returns regressed on SPY plus a market-orthogonalised US sector ETF; R-squared is the share a UCITS market-plus-sector combination reproduces. Where Yahoo's INDUSTRY has a covered index the narrower line is used -- semiconductor names are regressed on SMH rather than XLK, matching the fund named as their proxy.
single_name_decomposition.self_inclusion: The regressors hold the stock being decomposed, sometimes as one of their largest positions, so part of every share below is the position explaining itself. It bites hardest exactly where the number matters most, on the mega-caps, and it grew when the semiconductor regressor narrowed: NVDA reads 69.3% against a 25-stock semiconductor index, 63.5% against broad technology and 61.3% against the wider ICE Semiconductor index. The stock did not become more replicable; the benchmark became more like the stock.
single_name_decomposition.why_us_listed_proxies: Both regressors are US-listed. Cross-venue return differences carry a close-time artefact large enough to swamp this measurement -- it measured 6.03pp on a pair that genuinely tracks. The UCITS line is named separately as the thing to buy; it is not the thing being regressed.
single_name_decomposition.caveat: A variance share over one window, not a hedge ratio and not a forecast. A high figure does not make a sector fund a substitute; the concentration risk of a single name IS the residual.
